Technology stocks were edging lower Wednesday afternoon, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 index falling about 0.1% while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was off nearly 0.7%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Intelstat SA ( I ) soared to a four-year high on Wednesday, topping out with a nearly 21% advance, after Kerrisdale Advisers reported a 6.3% passive stake in the satellite services company, acquiring more than 8.6 million of its shares and explaining its long position in the company stock to a federal proposal to reallocate a portion of Intelstat's C band frequencies for additional wire spectrum for its new long position in the company's stock. Intelstat has proposed a market-based approach to the reallocation that would allow it and other C band users to put the spectrum up for sale while also transitioning their customers out of the band. The Federal Communications Commission is expected to make a decision on the C Band sale to provide additional bandwidth for 5G mobile use during the second half of 2019.
In other sector news:
- Baidu ( BIDU ) was losing ground in Wednesday trading, falling almost 2% in the afternoon, despite the Chinese-language search engine company earlier authorizing a $1 billion stock buyback program that will be implemented over the next 12 months. The company plans to fund repurchases from its existing cash balance.
- Determine Inc ( DTRM ) retreated on Wednesday, falling as much as 12%, after the software-as-a-service company reported a wider-than-expected Q4 net loss and revenue that fell short of analyst forecasts. Net loss during the three months ended March 31 tripled year-over-year to $0.12 per share compared with its $0.04 per share loss during the first three months in 2017 and missing the Capital IQ consensus expecting a $0.10 per share net loss. Revenue fell to $6.8 million from $7.5 million during the same period last year, lagging the $7.3 million Street view.
